one_liner: A three-year Air Force PALACE Acquire budget analyst internship (GS-7/9, promotes to GS-12) doing budget formulation, execution and cost analysis, ending in a permanent job.
fit_summary: Daniel may qualify on education: a master's degree is this posting's GS-9 route (one year of graduate study covers GS-7), if HR accepts Global Affairs as related to budget work. His pivot-table spending trackers for multi-state COVID-19 purchases are relevant budget experience, though the work itself is technical financial management rather than his core field.
eligibility: Hiring paths include the public, Pathways recent graduates, competitive federal employees and veterans, but the Summary sends you to the agency's eligibility page. Confirm the public path is open, since his 2016 M.A. rules out the recent-graduate path.

GS-7 requires one of these: 1 year of graduate education, a bachelor's with Superior Academic Achievement (GPA 2.95+, upper third of the class, or a national honor society), 5 years of pre-professional study, or 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-5.
GS-9 requires a master's degree, 2 years of graduate study, or a related LL.B/J.D.
You must be able to obtain a Secret clearance.
If you qualify on education, submit copies of all transcripts, including transferred hours. Degree audits are not accepted.
keywords: automated financial management databases and systems
strategy: Check the agency's eligibility page first (his 2016 degree won't count if recent-graduate status is required), then apply at GS-9 on education and upload his George Mason transcript.
You must apply through afciviliancareers.com/recentgraduates and finish the HireVue assessment. If you skip HireVue, you will not be considered.
Frame the IEM work around money and data: budgets, cost estimates, FEMA or grant funding tracking, spreadsheets and reporting, but only the parts you actually did. List hours per week for each job.
Keep the resume to two pages and use the posting's exact terms (budget formulation, budget execution, cost analysis). HR will not read cover letters or links.
On the questionnaire, rate yourself honestly but fully. If coursework or a job involved budgeting or data analysis, claim it and make sure the resume backs it up.
Prepare for the HireVue competencies (customer service, interpersonal skills, stress tolerance) with STAR stories from client work at IEM.
resume_bullets: Built Excel pivot-table reports on spending and order status for multi-state COVID-19 supply purchasing (2021–2022).
Helped sequence onboarding for FEMA Public Assistance employees by organizing spreadsheets and analyzing the data for decision makers (2019–2020).
Helped counties update their applications for COVID-19 emergency grants at the start of the pandemic (2020).
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you analyzed data and used it to make a recommendation.
How would you handle a tight deadline in which numbers from two sources don't match?
What do you know about the federal budget process, from formulation to execution?
Describe a time you had to learn a complex system or rules quickly.
watch_outs: The job may relocate you. Locations vary, travel is possible, and there is no telework, so you may not stay in Manassas.
Without the transcript he would need GS-5-level specialized budget experience; the M.A. is the simpler route, so attach it.
This is a quantitative role that makes limited use of your politics and public-facing strengths, so make sure the work itself appeals to you.
